RFC 2545 Section 3 read: "The value of the Length of Next Hop Network Address field on a MP_REACH_NLRI attribute shall be set to 16, when only a global address is present, or 32 if a link-local address is also included in the Next Hop field." The moved units (TestFamilyNextHopForwardAdmission, TestRFC2545EffectivePairPolicyAndMixedSibling) still compare the whole MP_REACH value, length octet included (0x10 for the global, 0x20 for an on-link pair, the pair trimmed to 0x10 off-link), and the VPN-shaped 24/48-octet and native-IPv4 fields now arrive as the export chain's raw answer and are still withdrawn, never sent at their wrong width. The superseded-* and later-repair positives now take the legal replacement from the destination's configured next hop over the raw base (the only producer of an edit after a raw answer); checkRFC2545NextHops changed only linkLocalAt to labconfig.LinkLocalAt, byte-identical arithmetic (fe80 + first six prefix octets + host). Verdict unchanged. e33567fb2d then reworded only tag prose, re-read: the RFC2545-3-2 positive now says the destination's configured next hop writes the legal 16- or 32-octet field over the obsolete one the export filter leaves, and the TestBuildRelayUpdateMarksRebuilt tags now name the external filter fields rebuilt and source-llgr-advertised; both now state exactly what the bodies assert, so the wording nits are resolved. Earlier judgement, still standing for the unmoved units: Re-judged 2026-11-02 by an independent auditor who authored none of 06b26570b6, e145f7bf39 or 0a030d3e7a. RFC 2545 Section 3 read: "The value of the Length of Next Hop Network Address field on a MP_REACH_NLRI attribute shall be set to 16, when only a global address is present, or 32 if a link-local address is also included in the Next Hop field." Units moved since the last verdict: TestFamilyNextHopOriginationAdmission (egressRouteFilter stub gained a nil follow-body return, ff89fc8110; assertions identical); internal/le/interoplab/bgp/check_rfc.go::checkRFC2545NextHops now calls labconfig.LinkLocalAt(check.Network.IPv6, zeHostNumber), byte-for-byte the same computation as the removed linkLocalAt (c782411791, diffed); TestRFC2545EffectivePairPolicyAndMixedSibling runs the route-server rail through the fast path's own export chain (06b26570b6) with the wire assertions unchanged, so wrong-width effective next hops (native IPv4, VPN 24 and 48 shapes, including a 48-octet pair whose off-link trim would hide its width) still cannot leave under IPv6 unicast, and a later legal 16- or 32-octet replacement is sent with its exact bytes. The limit recorded before stands: no recorded break isolates the octet write itself, because the octet and the field share one source and the writer gate refuses a malformed attribute; the exact-byte positives would fail if a mismatched octet reached the wire.
